# Perception — Extract Threat Intelligence

## Purpose

Make the threat intelligence Perception has **already extracted** (usually by someone else, usually already paid for) searchable and usable here: *what was analyzed recently, is topic X covered, show me the report, turn it into hunts and detections.* Reading existing sessions is **free on the Perception side and changes nothing in the tenant**. If the article was never analyzed (or the user hands over a new URL), this skill can request a fresh `analyze-article` run: **always asked first, with the cost shown** (Phase 7).

Positioning: *Perception extracts; this repo verifies, hunts and authors detections.* It **complements** `threat-intel-campaign` (feed-based hunts), `detection-authoring` (rules) and `ioc-investigation` (indicators).

**Read first:** [`.github/skills/perception-shared/REFERENCE.md`](../perception-shared/REFERENCE.md) (§3.7 cache, §5 validation, §6 evidence, §9 links). Helper: [`session_cache.py`](../perception-shared/session_cache.py).

**Entity (any of):** a **topic or keyword**, an article **title**, a Threat Analytics **portal link** (`…/threatanalytics3/<guid>/overview`: the GUID is the article ID), an internal article ID + title, a Perception **session ID**, **any article or advisory URL** (vendor blog, CISA/IC3 advisory: reused if already analyzed, otherwise Phase 7), or a request to **list the articles Perception analyzed recently** (the card's *recent articles* checkbox sends exactly that; typing `recent` works too).

**Where intelligence comes from:** any finished session whose input is a threat-intelligence article carries a `threat_intelligence_report.md` from the same Threat Intelligence Agent: `analyze-article` (TI only), `proactive-protection`, `detect-emerging-threats`. All three are valid sources.

---

## Workflow

### Phase 0 — Preconditions
**🔴 MCP GATE — do this before reading the session cache, the index, saved reports, `reports/`, or Mission Control findings.** Check that `perception-mcp-*` tools are available (use the tool search tool; they are deferred). **If they are not: your reply MUST begin with the setup guidance** — *"The Perception MCP isn't configured in this session. Add an HTTP MCP server for `https://perception.microsoft.com/mcp` (e.g. `.mcp.json`: `\"perception-mcp\": { \"type\": \"http\", \"url\": \"https://perception.microsoft.com/mcp\" }`), sign in, reload MCP servers and retry. Needs Perception enabled in the tenant and Security Reader or higher. (Docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/agentic-security/agentic-security-mcp — it lists `https://perception.microsoft.com/mcp`; the `sentinel.microsoft.com` URL above also responds.)"* After the guidance you may *offer* a **read-only search of the existing local cache** and saved reports, labeled "saved result, not refreshed/re-validated — Perception MCP unavailable" `[asserted]`. **In this offline mode you must NOT refresh or write the cache, write or edit any report, post a Mission Control finding, run new analysis queries, or suggest follow-ups that need fresh Perception data.** Full rules: REFERENCE §1.1. Then state the tenant.

### Phase 1 — Refresh the session cache (REFERENCE §3.7)
`list_sessions(pageSize=100)` → `session_cache.py ingest <saved file>`; follow `CONTINUE` / `STOP` exactly (token passed **unchanged**, `--continue` on later pages, 10-page cap). The first build of a busy tenant covers only ~1-3 days per few pages: say how far back it reaches. Never read raw pages into chat. Skip the refresh only if the cache was refreshed in this conversation already.

### Phase 2 — Answer the question from the cache
- **"recent / what was analyzed":** `search --ti-only --articles --limit 15`.
- **Topic / keyword:** `search <terms> --ti-only --articles`. **Answer from what is cached first** (titles plus any cached summaries) and quote the header's *summaries cached for X of Y articles*. Titles are often not enough ("supply chain" vs a package name). If X < Y, tell the user how many articles are unsearched by content and **read summaries in one bounded batch**: `need-summary --ti-only --limit 12` (newest first), call `get_session_summary` for all of them **in parallel**, write **one** JSON file of condensed, keyword-rich lines (threat, techniques, malware/tool names, sectors) with the `create` tool and store it with **one** `set-many <file>` call, then search again. Do not fetch more than 12 per request; if articles remain unchecked say how many and offer to continue. This cost is **one-time**: summaries persist, later refreshes only add the few new articles, and a warm cache makes topic search instant. A user may ask to "warm the topic index": then loop the batch until `coverage` shows no articles missing.
- **Specific article (title / portal link / ID / other URL):** for a non-portal URL search for a distinctive fragment of it (host + path, no query string); sessions started from a URL keep it as the article title/URL, and a `.pdf` and a `.csv` of the same advisory are different inputs. **URL title fallback (REFERENCE §3.6):** the same article is often analyzed under a different title or as an internal Threat Analytics article (Activity Profile), so a URL-only match is not enough. **Also** search the **slug words** (last path segment split on hyphens, a trailing `-2` or digits dropped, e.g. `search "high volume phishing campaign microsoft 365 outage lures"`; the raw hyphenated slug matches nothing). Offer title-matched runs as *probable same article, not an exact URL match* and ask the user to confirm before reuse; show URL-started runs next to them with their outcome (a run can be `succeeded` yet empty, so validate with `list_outputs`).  `search "<title words>"`; a portal link's GUID can be matched against `articleId` (`show <id>`). If nothing matches, say so **with the cache depth**; do **not** guess an ID. Offer: have the user start it from the Threat Analytics page in the Defender portal (then give you the session ID), or an explicit new run (Phase 7).
- Present the article list as a table: article title, latest run, number of sessions, playbooks, best session (`id8`, linked per REFERENCE §9), whether a summary is cached. Many sessions for one article are normal (other users, tests, re-runs); the best candidate is the newest **validated** one. Put a session in the *best session* column only if it passed REFERENCE §5; when every run of an article failed or is report-less, write *none usable* and give the reason instead of linking a session.
- Free-form questions about **what Perception has done** beyond articles (e.g. incident sessions) can use the same cache (`search --playbook investigate-incident`) but are out of scope for presentation here.

### Phase 3 — Select and validate a source session
For the chosen session: `get_session`, `list_agent_runs`, `list_outputs` (REFERENCE §5). Require a real `threat_intelligence_report.md`. **Session status is not proof either way:** a run that is `failed`/`stopped` or still `running` keeps the TI report if it got past the Threat Intelligence step (a Protect run cancelled later still has it), so check `list_outputs` for every candidate and never write "failed, no report" from the status alone (the cache search and `need-summary` already include such sessions). `status: succeeded` with only an audit log or a summary means the article retrieval failed: discard it, say why, try the next candidate or report that no usable report exists (`set <id> --ti-report no`). Record good ones with `--ti-report yes`. Prefer the newest validated report; mention the initiator (it may be another user in the tenant) and the report date.

### Phase 4 — Present the report
`read_output` the report (large: the tool saves it to a file; parse that file, do not paste it). Save a verbatim copy to `reports/perception/extract-threat-intel/<slug>_<yyyymmdd>/threat_intelligence_report.md` (gitignored) and write this skill's report next to it as `report.md`. Topic, recent-articles, verification and detection-draft answers are flat files in `reports/perception/extract-threat-intel/` (`<topic>_<yyyymmdd>.md`, `recent_articles_<yyyymmdd>.md`, `<slug>_verification_<yyyymmdd>.md`, `cd_draft_<slug>_<yyyymmdd>.md`); layout in REFERENCE §7. Present, tagging claims `[perception: session <id8>]` (= `[asserted]`), every session link clickable (REFERENCE §9):
1. **Header:** article title, the `**Perception session:** [🔗 Open session …]` line (REFERENCE §9; run `session_cache.py check-links <report.md> --fix` on every report you write, exit 0 required), run date/initiator, report age, cost note (*read from an existing run: no new Perception spend*).
2. **Threat summary** and actors (say *unattributed* if the report does).
3. **TTP table**, keeping **Tactic / Technique / Detection opportunity / Telemetry** (condense the rest).
4. **Indicators** table, and the **TI-platform (TIP) coverage table**: rows reading *Check failed / Try again* are a **gap, not coverage**: say so and offer to re-check later or sweep the indicators in this tenant.
5. **Hunting queries** exactly as written, labeled `[asserted]` until Phase 5.
6. **Recommended actions** re-rendered as portal paths and plain-language steps (REFERENCE §8): no state-changing commands.
7. **Limits:** what the report says it could not retrieve or check; the article's own date (an old article may be stale).

### Phase 5 — Verify against the tenant (automatic; REFERENCE §6)
Run Perception's hunting queries and an IOC sweep here (bounded, read-only; ask only for Data Lake / lookbacks over 30 d). Follow the repo's KQL pre-flight (manifest/grep first, schema check, Step 0 tool choice: Advanced Hunting ≤ 30 d, Data Lake otherwise, bounded `take`/`summarize`, **execute before sharing**). Report results as `[verified: <table>, <window>]`; "not seen in this tenant" is a valid result; zero results from a possibly bad query must be sanity-checked (Step 5). If a query uses a table that does not exist in the chosen tool, or the tool throttles or drops, say so and do not loop.

### Phase 6 — Hand-off (this is where the intelligence becomes work)
Offer, per user choice; this skill never writes or deploys a detection itself:
- **Detections:** for each TTP row the user picks, build a *seed* (technique + ID, the report's **Detection opportunity**, **Telemetry**, relevant indicators, Perception's hunting query) and hand it to `kql-query-authoring` (use its custom-detection intent) → `detection-authoring` (author-only → manifest → **Detection Wizard link** via `wizard_link.py from-manifest`; Graph deploy only on explicit deploy wording).
- **Hunts:** `threat-intel-campaign` with the article (title/link) and this report path as context.
- **Indicators:** `ioc-investigation` for chosen indicators.
- **Deeper run:** if the user also wants tenant-aware detections and posture, point to `perception-protect-against-threat` (an existing Protect run may already exist: the cache shows it); its cost is far higher, so show the estimate (REFERENCE §1.3).

### Phase 7 — Optional: start a new `analyze-article` run (only on explicit request)
Use when the cache has nothing for the article or URL **and** the user asks to analyze it (or to re-run). Never start from a topic keyword alone. **First** search the cache for the same article/URL **and its slug words** (Phase 1 URL title fallback) and offer the existing run (it costs nothing); never say "no usable run" from a URL-only search.

**Inputs (REFERENCE §2), pick by what the user gave:**
| User gave | Input | Reliability |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| Threat Analytics article (portal link `…/threatanalytics3/<guid>/overview`, or ID + title) | `values:["<id>"]` + `displayName:"<exact title>"`; for a portal link the GUID is the ID, the title comes from the cache or REFERENCE §3.6 (ask the user if neither has it) | Reliable |
| Any other `https://` URL (vendor blog, advisory) | one URL in `values:["<url>"]`, no `displayName` | **Best-effort**: results in this tenant are mixed (some URLs gave a full report, others only an audit log, an empty report or a `failed`/`stopped` run). Say so before asking |

Accept `https://` URLs only (refuse `http:`, `file:` and local paths, and start nothing). For a PDF or CSV URL, mention that the HTML landing page may work better if the first attempt comes back empty.

**Confirm first (REFERENCE §1.3):** the URL or article, the estimated Perception cost **≈ $3.89–$6.80** (TI report, snapshot 2026-11-19, not a quote), ≈ 4 minutes, the agent identity, and for a free-form URL that an empty result is possible and that billing of an empty run is not visible through the MCP. Start only after an explicit yes. Then `list_playbooks` → `start_session` (`analyze-article`, `inputs:[{key:"article", type:"defenderThreatIntelligenceId", values:[…], displayName?}]`). Poll (REFERENCE §4), validate with `list_outputs` (§5), then continue at Phase 3. If the run is empty, say so, record it (`set <id> --ti-report no` after the next refresh) and offer **one** alternative (a different URL for the same content); never retry automatically. The new session joins the cache on the next refresh.

### Phase 8 — Record
If launched from Mission Control **and** a specific article's (or a topic's matched articles') intelligence was presented, post a finding tagged `[perception: session <id8>]` (or `[perception: cache of N sessions]` for a multi-article topic; treated as `[asserted]`): article(s), report date, TTP/indicator counts, TIP gaps, verification results, hand-off follow-ups. Do **not** post a finding for pure "what was analyzed recently" listings.
**Severity is `info` unless an active threat is found in this tenant. Check this before posting: the finding's `severity` and every metric's `severity` must be `info`/`clean`/null unless Phase 5 produced matching tenant evidence; a metric lifted from Perception's own report or recon (for example "10 users lack MFA") is `[asserted]` and must not carry `medium`/`high`.** A finding that rests only on Perception's report, or on a tenant check that came back clean, stays `info` (a clean verification may use `clean`). Raise it only for what Phase 5 actually found: `low` for exposure without activity (for example an affected package version present in an inventory), `medium` or `high` only for matching indicators or activity in the tenant (`high` needs two or more concrete findings, per the repo's evidence rule). The threat's severity in the world is not the finding's severity here.
**Scope note:** this skill's subject is the threat-intelligence report. A topic answer may add one line of context from the same session's `summary.md` (for example that a Protect run also produced detections), clearly tagged, but must not present Recon/Detection/Posture content as threat intelligence or as tenant evidence; send those to `perception-protect-against-threat`/`perception-tune-detection`. So do **not** add a section summarizing the Recon result, candidate accounts or tenant exposure from a Protect run, and do not put its accounts in the finding's entities: say in one line that the run also produced a recon/detection/posture report and name the skill that reads it.

---

## Guardrails
- Reading existing sessions needs no confirmation; **starting** a session always does (never automatic; cost shown; never from a bare keyword). Refuse `red-web-pentest` / `find-fix-web-app-security-risks` outright, without asking for a target (REFERENCE §1.4).
- Cache answers must state their depth; never claim "no article covers X" without it. Never invent an article ID.
- Sessions from other users are readable and fair game; name the initiator, don't speculate about them.
- Perception output is `[perception: session …]` until re-queried here (then `[verified]`); apply the REFERENCE §6 claim split (tenant observation vs Perception's assessment). Hunting queries are hypotheses until executed.
- No tenant identifiers in tracked files; cache, reports and index stay in gitignored paths (`temp/`, `reports/perception/extract-threat-intel/`).
- Remediation as portal paths only (REFERENCE §8). Nothing is deployed by this skill.
